AgenticWorkspace.description:
A workspace in which an AI agent can re-run an Activity, plus the prompt that asks it to. This is the agentic counterpart of the executable provenance an Activity already carries: `command` and `container_image` tell a machine how to replay a step, while `regeneration_prompt` and `workspace_url` tell an agent how to.
It is typed `prov:Plan` because that is what it is in PROV terms — a description of intended execution, not the execution itself. The run remains the Activity; this is the recipe the agent follows. Keeping them separate matters: re-running a plan produces a NEW Activity, and conflating the two would make a regenerated result indistinguishable from the original.
WARNING ON REPRODUCIBILITY. A prompt is not a deterministic replay mechanism. The same prompt, workspace, and model can yield a different result run to run. Treat `regeneration_prompt` as documentation of intent that a human or agent can act on, NOT as a guarantee of bit-identical output — that is what `command` plus `container_image` plus `code_version` are for. Record the model and version actually used so a divergent re-run can at least be explained.

agent_model.description: Model that ran, or is expected to run, the prompt (e.g. "claude-fable-5"). Recorded so a divergent re-run can be explained.

regeneration_prompt.description: The prompt that asks an agent to regenerate this analysis. Write it self-contained: an agent opening the workspace cold should be able to act on it without the surrounding conversation.

workspace_url.description: Resolvable URL for the workspace — where a person or agent goes to open it. In the example of akleao this is a fork URL, `https://www.akleao.com/fork/<slug-id>`: one shareable link that opens the workspace, rather than a path through project and branch ids. Required in spirit: a workspace nobody can reach is not provenance, it is a note.

CellState.description: A cellular phenotype defined by the combination of GenePrograms active in a cell (or cell population) — e.g. "activated", "exhausted", "hypoxic". Mixes in `ProvenancedResource` so a CellState is citable and attributable the same way a `GeneProgram` (via `Set`) already is.

GeneProgram.description: A Set whose members are genes that co-vary as a coordinated unit and together carry out a biological process — a factor from matrix factorization (cNMF, NMF, Spectra, WGCNA) or a curated gene module. No ontology term is asserted as class_uri — none resolves to "gene program" / "gene expression program" (verified against EBI OLS4) — so GeneProgram grounds via `is_a: Set` (prov:Collection), the same way GeneSet does. Distinct from GeneSet: a GeneSet is typically a static annotation (e.g. an MSigDB term); a GeneProgram is inferred from expression covariance and is usually a quantitative loading over genes, not just membership. `member_weights`, when present, is that loading — one number per gene in `members`, positionally paired. A very large loading matrix should still reference its source file via the member-manifest escape hatch `Set` already provides rather than enumerate weights here.

Set.description: A collection of members — "an entity that provides a structure to some constituents, which are themselves entities" (prov:Collection). Set is deliberately separate from Dataset: a Dataset is a set of *data* (schema:Dataset); a Set is a set of *things* (genes, proteins, variants). Members are referenced via `prov:hadMember`. Set carries the same attribution/provenance/mirror slots (ProvenancedResource) as Dataset, so a returned set is citable and its authoritative provenance is mirror-protected identically.
